| admission-lib | writer | manual | no | none | OBSERVE MODE ONLY -- NOT an enforcement mechanism. blocking:false is literal: adm_admit's final statement is an unconditional return 0 and Scenario 15 fails the suite if any input combination produces non-zero. The flip is T6, gated on >=7 days of ledger plus operator sign-off. STATE OF THE DELIVERABLE AFTER THE 2026-07-28 REVIEW ROUND (harness-reviewer REJECT-amend-forward + task-verifier FAIL, both on commit f6562b2; amended in the follow-up commit): the ledger as originally shipped was NOT recording what this entry claimed. Two Critical parser defects -- adm_live_sessions read a live_sessions key estate-janitor.sh NEVER writes, and both extractors stripped to end-of-line against a producer that emits the whole snapshot as ONE line (a true 3 parsed as 3379, which at T6 would have blocked every dispatch) -- plus an uninterpretable kind:"0" label on the highest-volume source. All 14 pre-fix production lines were archived to state/governor/discarded/ and the >=7-day clock restarted from the fixed build. RETIRED CLAIMS (this slice's program-rule-3 retirement -- rule 3 permits retiring a hook, store, OR CLAIM, and task-verifier correctly noted the claim column was the one available): (a) the 'spawn-free hot path / forks at most ONCE / ~0 ms' claim, refuted by two independent measurements (19.3 ms and 20.1 ms per dispatch, ~45 forks, 2 execs) and replaced with the measured numbers plus a <5 ms T6 budget; (b) the absolute 'nothing here trusts a caller-supplied claim' claim, refuted because the lib is SOURCED into the dispatcher's shell -- ADM_ABSURD_SESSION_CAP, ADM_ESTATE_SNAPSHOT and especially ADM_STATE_DIR (which hides the HALT kill switch entirely) are environment bypasses, now PINNED by Scenario 10b so T6 cannot flip enforcement believing they are closed. The accurate claim is 'no caller ARGUMENT decides'. COVERAGE: Task/Agent/Workflow dispatch; session-resumer resume, fresh-spawn AND storm-cap-queued deferrals (that early return previously emitted nothing -- silence exactly during the storms this slice exists to characterize); spawn-worktree creates. NOT COVERED: Decision-011 cloud/scheduled sessions, a human running claude directly, MCP-side agent spawns -- unmeasured load when reading calibration. Not event-wired in settings.json.template -- a sourced lib with four one-line splices inside already-wired scripts; manifest-check's disk scan only walks top-level hooks/*.sh, never hooks/lib/, so this entry is inventory-for-honesty, not enforcement. |
| agent-commit-gate | gate | SubagentStop | no | none | — |
| agent-design-gate | gate | PreToolUse | no | pretool | — |
| agent-heartbeat | writer | — | no | none | scripts/agent-heartbeat.sh (emit/conclude/watch/reap) — per-AGENT liveness heartbeat in the heartbeats/agents/ namespace (2026-07-14 lesson: background agents need a push heartbeat + watchdog, not orchestrator output-polling). watch AND reap are spliced into hooks/stalled-work-surfacer.sh run() (watch surfaces stalled agents at SessionStart alongside stalled Workflow runs; reap bounds the namespace — the session-heartbeat reaper's 2026-07-09 dead-reaper defect, avoided here by wiring reap in the same commit). conclude is the terminal beat: an agent self-removes on clean completion so a COMPLETED agent is never surfaced as stalled (mirrors the workflow half's started==result suppression; without it every finished agent false-fires — the cry-wolf that REFORMULATE'd orphaned-worktree-guard, fixed here per harness-review CONDITIONAL-PASS 2026-07-14). INTERIM PATTERN: relies on the dispatched agent calling emit/conclude (dispatch-prompt convention in doctrine/background-work-tracking.md); the true runtime auto-heartbeat is not in-repo. Detection covers agents that emitted then stopped (the worked-then-wedged class). Not event-wired as its own settings.json entry — a splice inside the already-wired stalled-work-surfacer.sh; inventory-only per the manifest-check disk-coverage note (scripts/ is not disk-scanned). |

(2) GATE 2 = the 'agent-design-gate' entry (adapters/claude-code/hooks/agent-design-gate.sh): PreToolUse on Edit|Write|MultiEdit, blocks a brand-new adapters/claude-code/agents/*.md Write lacking a '## GOLDEN CASE' section + evidence of the seven properties; grandfathers all pre-bar agents by on-disk-existence check; 7/7 self-test scenarios. Operator directive 2026-07-14. |
| ask-registry | writer | — | no | none | scripts/ask-registry.sh — the ask-registry CLI (register/attach-session/link-plan/set-status/merge/override-project, plus the cockpit-roadmap-redesign Task 2 work-item-layer verbs: set-title/capture-candidate/classify-candidate/detach-candidate/amend, PLUS the accountable-estate-program-2026-07 Task 2 ask-SLA verbs: set-deadline/clear-deadline/set-default-action/sla) writing ~/.claude/state/ask-registry.jsonl plus a best-effort in-repo mirror at docs/asks/ask-registry.jsonl (path resolved via nl_main_checkout_root, never a worktree) and a heuristic-first summarizer (ASK_SUMMARIZER=haiku upgrade, async, best-effort; the SAME gated async lane classifies amendment candidates amendment/noise — best-effort, candidates stay honestly pending on any failure). Round-6-gap-5 follow-on fix (cockpit-roadmap-redesign): the flag was proven dormant in production (grep found zero exporters anywhere) — hooks/workstreams-read.sh's ASK-CAPTURE SPLICE now defaults it to "haiku" mechanically for every real (non-HARNESS_SELFTEST) register/capture-candidate call, so the lane runs without anyone remembering to export it; an operator can still override to any other value ahead of a session. Title records carry title_source auto|operator; readers MUST fold operator-beats-auto regardless of timestamp (the A3 precedence contract in the script header). Deadline records carry a matching carve-out (DEADLINE FOLD, script header SCHEMA section): a reader folds ONLY deadline_set/deadline_cleared records by ts and takes the latest, since plain last-non-empty-wins can never represent an explicit clear; default_action has no such carve-out (plain last-non-empty-wins). set-deadline validates + normalizes to canonical %Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ before storing (rejects unparseable input, no-op); set-default-action stores a disposition AS DATA ONLY this slice (no automatic enforcement reads it yet, per the program's observe-first rule); sla is a read-only TSV read-out (overdue|due-soon|ok|no-deadline, sorted soonest-first) consumed manually and by estate-janitor.sh's ask-fold (which folds the same deadline/default_action fields into snapshot.json for estate-brief.sh's SLA panel — see the estate-janitor/estate-brief manifest entries). Called by hooks/workstreams-read.sh's capture splices (register on the first operator prompt; capture-candidate on every later prompt of an ask-attached session — both guarded by hooks/lib/progress-log-lib.sh's pl_classify_session against spawned/builder sessions) and by hooks/session-start-digest.sh's session-attach splice (attach-session, beside the existing heartbeat splice); set-status/merge are also called by the workstreams-ui server's POST /api/ask/<id>/lifecycle endpoint (operator override) and by the background auditor (mechanical completion). Not event-wired as its own settings.json entry — a one-line splice call-site inside already-wired hooks, mirroring the session-heartbeat/ensure-cockpit convention. Inventory-only per the filed nl-issue note that manifest-check's disk-coverage check (b) only disk-scans hooks/*.sh top-level, never scripts/ — this entry exists for honesty, not enforcement. 2026-07-30 DETERMINISTIC-CLASSIFIER UPDATE (URGENT operator-facing defect fix, docs/plans/requests-tab-visibility-fix-2026-07-30.md): the ASK_SUMMARIZER=haiku LLM classify lane described above is PROVEN DEAD in production -- `claude --model haiku -p ...` invoked from a hook running inside an already-live Claude Code session does not fail fast, it hangs until nl_run_bounded's 20s bound kills it (reproduced directly), so zero of 114 real amendment_candidate records captured 2026-07-28..30 on this machine ever got a candidate_classified verdict. A NEW deterministic classifier (no model call, no network, no hang risk) now runs UNCONDITIONALLY on every capture-candidate call via neural-lace/workstreams-ui/server/verbatim-resolver.js, which resolves the operator's REAL prompt text from their own Claude Code session transcript (timestamp-nearest matching, validated against the 114 real records) and classifies by lexical overlap. `_AR_VALID_CLASSIFICATIONS` gained a fourth value, `promoted`: a candidate substantively unrelated to its parent ask is spun off into its OWN new top-level ask via `cmd_register`, instead of staying buried as a pending amendment forever. The LLM lane above is now invoked ONLY as a sequential fallback INSIDE the deterministic classifier's own subshell, when its resolution genuinely fails -- never as a second, independently-scheduled writer racing it on the same candidate_id fold key (see `_ar_async_deterministic_classify_candidate`'s own LANE SEQUENCING comment in the script). A new read-only `heuristic-summarize` verb (`cmd_heuristic_summarize`) exposes the existing summarizer for `adapters/claude-code/scripts/backfill-classify-amendment-candidates.sh`, a new one-shot idempotent script that retroactively classifies the pre-existing stuck-pending candidates against a copy of the registry (never writes to it directly -- delegates to this script's own classify-candidate/register verbs). |

PowerShell aliases for Get-ChildItem (`gci`, `ls`, `dir`) are not recognized, only the literal cmdlet name. `find`'s pre-path global options are handled for the common set (-H/-L/-P/-O0..3/-D) — an unrecognized one placed before the root could shift the parse. |

CHOKEPOINT: pre-commit-gate.sh -> plan-reviewer.sh Check 19. SCOPE (the blocking claim is deliberately narrow): BLOCKS a plan not already ACTIVE in HEAD (new plans, and DRAFT->ACTIVE flips); WARNs on plans already ACTIVE in HEAD; SKIPs non-ACTIVE plans and any plan outside a repository; UNDECIDABLE currently WARNs rather than blocks (warn-mode cycle, see retirement_condition). BYPASS PATHS (enumerated mechanically, not by reading — the first draft listed 4 and adversarial review found 3 more): (1) commit with --no-verify - NAMED-AND-ACCEPTED, closing it needs server-side enforcement this estate lacks. (2) `git -C <dir> commit` and other invocation shapes that do not match the settings.json.template PreToolUse matcher regex - NAMED-AND-ACCEPTED, verified NO-MATCH against the literal regex, and no real .git/hooks/pre-commit exists behind it; this defeats the whole pre-commit-gate chain and is not this unit's to fix. (3) Status other than ACTIVE - CLOSED-BY-DESIGN as SKIP: pre-ACTIVE iteration is never blocked, matching check17-draft-status-exempt. (4) DRAFT-commit then flip to ACTIVE - CLOSED: the grandfather is a CONTENT test (was the HEAD version ACTIVE, or did it already carry the section?), not a path-presence test, so the flip is treated as a new ACTIVE plan. Covered by self-test ee4. (5) Reword until the checker ACCEPTs - OPEN, NOT CLOSED, and the cost is ONE APPENDED CLAUSE, not determination. Appending a clause about what the artifact DOES satisfies the state-change test and vetoes the restatement rule: 'The gate is wired into pre-commit and blocks bad commits for the team.' -> ACCEPT, and 'The hook is registered in settings.json and starts on every user session.' -> ACCEPT - both opening with WRONG examples from the doctrine page itself. The obvious closure (require the change verb's subject to BE the human referent) was REJECTED because it false-blocks legitimate outcomes whose subject is a thing ('my work continues without me touching anything'). A mechanical vocabulary matcher cannot decide this class; this one raises the floor rather than closing the door. functionality-verifier STEP ZERO is the compensating judgement layer. (6) Plans already ACTIVE in HEAD - CLOSED-BY-DESIGN as WARN-only: blocking 46 pre-existing plans on next edit is the trust-erosion shape that turns a Mechanism into an override habit. (7) if-statement-check.sh absent, or exiting outside {0,1,2} - NAMED-AND-ACCEPTED: fails OPEN with a loud WARN. A checker that is missing or crashed is a harness defect, not a plan defect, and must not be reported to a builder as one. | operator-requirement-ledger | pattern | — | no | none | PATTERN over a MECHANISM -- rung stated plainly per constitution section 10; NO hook fires this, and none is claimed. MECHANICAL AND SELF-TESTED: the store (3 record types -- requirement_recorded / invariant_declared / invariant_verdict -- on the EXISTING ask-registry.jsonl, no new store, per the <=3-store consolidation goal, F5/F6 of docs/reviews/2026-07-27-accountable-estate-architecture-review.md); verbatim preservation (record-requirement bypasses _ar_truncate140, whose sentence-splitting and ellipsising IS the lossy step the ledger exists to prevent -- a 4000-CHARACTER cap only, and when that cap fires the stored value carries an explicit [TRUNCATED: N chars omitted] sentinel so a clipped paste can never be mistaken for a complete requirement); a NON-EMPTY ask_id enforced at the ONE writer (_ar_append_record refuses the append outright, so no present or future verb can create the empty-id record that collapses, under every reader's group_by(.ask_id), into a single phantom ask that can never be closed and never ages out); REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY (declare-invariant and invariant-verdict both refuse a --requirement-id naming no requirement_recorded, which used to be accepted, confirmed with a printed inv-1, and then be invisible to BOTH selectors task-verifier uses -- so invariant-check reported exit 3 nothing-registered and the verifier proceeded past a silently-dropped clause); the all-invariants-must-hold fold (last verdict wins per (requirement_id, invariant_id) sorted by [ts, append-index]; ABSENCE folds to `unverified`, never to a pass); the refusal of a `holds` verdict carrying no --evidence, no NON-WHITESPACE evidence (a blank-after-trim citation renders byte-identically to an unverified row, because the reader normalises ^ *$ to -), or evidence that could not be a citation in any reading (a purely SYNTACTIC shape test -- a : followed by a digit, a 7+ char hex SHA, or a / -- deliberately not a semantic quality judgement, which would over-fire); FOLD-FIELD ABSTENTION (all three record types leave EMPTY every field any reader folds last-non-empty-wins -- repo, project, verbatim_ref, status, summary, title_source, the list enumerated FROM the readers at derive-lib.js:110, auditor.js:302 and requests-routes.js:148 -- so a ledger record can rewrite neither the ask's cockpit title NOR its pointer to the original operator prompt; record-requirement no longer accepts --verbatim-ref at all); a FAILED READ IS NOT AN EMPTY READ (every jq reader over this store -- _ar_invariant_rows, cmd_invariants, cmd_sla -- captures jq's exit status and returns 4 CANNOT-EVALUATE, because discarding it meant one torn JSONL line produced an empty row set that invariant-check reported as exit 3 nothing-registered, converting a `violated` invariant into a silent pass; and the ROUTER now propagates that code with `exit $?` for all three read verbs -- `sla` was still routed `exit 0` like a write verb, which left the new guard inert at the CLI, the only surface anything actually calls, while the in-process self-test assertion stayed green: the SUBPROCESS assertion is the one that counts); and the invariant-check exit-code contract -- 0 all hold / 1 unmet / 3 nothing registered / 4 cannot evaluate, where 3 and 4 are deliberately NOT passes because 'a check that reports green because it never ran' is the failure class itself. NOT MECHANICAL, AND THIS IS THE HONEST GAP: nothing forces an agent to run record-requirement in the first place, and nothing forces task-verifier to execute its Step 1.6 -- both are protocol text. Automatic extraction from the prompt stream was deliberately NOT built: that is the retired goal-extraction-on-prompt.sh / goal-coverage-on-stop.sh narrative-gate class (ADR 058 D5, 'artifact checks block; narrative checks observe'), and rebuilding it would repeat a lesson this harness already paid for. No new blocking gate either -- 36 blocking entries exist against ADR 058 D5's <=12 target. MEASUREMENTS (quoted as DELTAS measured on ONE tree -- branch wip/harness-hardening-2026-07-29 at 417c434 -- because an earlier revision of this entry quoted absolute counts taken on a different tree, which the harness-reviewer correctly caught; absolute numbers here are meaningless without the tree they were taken on): 23 scenarios (RL1-RL23). BEFORE this fix round, on that tree: 72 passed / 5 failed. AFTER: 97 passed / 5 failed. Delta +25 passes, +0 failures -- IDENTICAL on both /opt/homebrew/bin/bash 5.3.15 and /bin/bash 3.2.57, and the 5 failures are the SAME five by identity as well as by count (PRE-EXISTING BSD-`date` failures in the unrelated set-deadline verb, untouched here). The 7 defects fixed in this round are each guarded by a scenario mutation-tested on BOTH interpreters -- the fix is reverted IN PLACE (a copy under /tmp scores differently, since the self-test's repo-root/mirror resolution depends on the script's own location, so an out-of-tree mutation run would prove nothing), each mutation is a semantically-valid reversion guarded by `bash -n` so syntax corruption cannot pass as a discriminating result, and each is asserted to apply exactly N times so a silently no-op'd mutation cannot yield a green run. Mapping mutation -> scenario turned RED: C1-writer -> RL17, C1-resolve -> RL18, C2-jq-status -> RL19, C3-refint -> RL20, M4-evidence -> RL21, M5-truncmark -> RL22, M6-verbatimref -> RL8. Every self-test fixture is produced by the real verbs -- no hand-written JSONL is fed to the reader. Not event-wired in settings.json.template; manifest-check's disk scan covers only top-level hooks/*.sh, never scripts/, so this entry exists for honesty, not enforcement. |

C2 the dead fail-safe above. (3) SUBJECT-SET ENUMERATION, BY DIFF CODE RATHER THAN BY VERB (completed 2026-07-30, harness-reviewer CRITICAL 1 round 3). 'The enforcing file is gone from its enforcing path' is ONE OUTCOME reachable by FOUR VERBS, and `git diff` scores each differently: edit=M, `git rm`=D, `git mv`=R100 <old> <new> (so --diff-filter=ACMR emits ONLY THE DESTINATION and --diff-filter=D emits NOTHING), typechange=T (excluded by BOTH). The first round closed only D, leaving `git mv` and typechange PROVEN-open: against a real bare remote with the live gate as the pre-push hook, `git mv adapters/claude-code/hooks/victim-gate.sh docs/victim-gate.sh` pushed rc=0 with ZERO gate bytes and the path GONE from the remote, and a regular-file->symlink typechange pushed rc=0 leaving the remote carrying mode 120000. Both are now closed by two tokens: --diff-filter=ACMRT on the changed-file enumeration, and --no-renames on the deletion enumeration (which forces a rename's SOURCE to be reported as a plain D instead of being folded into an R pair). GENERALIZATION, stated so it outlives this gate: every gate deriving a subject set from `git diff` must enumerate by the codes through which its subject can change OR LEAVE the surface, never by a hand-listed set of verbs; and every new self-test carries a `git mv` case and a typechange case BESIDE its `git rm` case. FP COST, RE-MEASURED INDEPENDENTLY over all 1763 master commits rather than inherited: deletions 8 commits (0.45%) / 104 files; rename sources +7 commits (0.40%) / +38 files; typechanges 0 commits / 0 files (free). The rename figure is deliberately reported as 38/7 and not the 37/6 (0.34%) that the review cited: 37 files across 6 commits are renames OUT of the surface, but one further case is a rename WITHIN it (adapters/claude-code/rules/conversation-tree-state.md -> rules/workstreams-state.md, commit e272c3e), which --no-renames also flags and which the narrower framing omitted. It is NOT suppressed: adding a 'source vanished but destination is in-surface' exemption would put an escape branch inside the very control that exists to make vanishing hard, to save one commit in 1763. Total bill for the new arms is therefore 0.40%, still cheaper than the 0.45% deletion arm already accepted. Those pushes need the operator override, which is the intended price of making 'move the gate' and 'retype the gate' as hard as 'edit the gate'. Suite counts on BOTH /bin/bash 3.2.57 and /opt/homebrew/bin/bash 5.3.15, identical on each (re-derive: `bash adapters/claude-code/hooks/review-record-push-gate.sh --self-test | tail -2` and the same for hooks/lib/review-record-gate-lib.sh): this gate 53/0 (was 43/0, was 28/0), hooks/lib/review-record-gate-lib.sh 75/0 (was 67/0, was 43/0). SIX mutation proofs guard the six independent controls, each RE-CONFIRMED to make its own attack pass again when the control is removed: Scenario 15 (neuter the block decision -> golden case wrongly passes), Scenario 19b (delete the git-hooks/* surface arm -> the unreviewed-dispatcher push wrongly passes), Scenario 20 (revert the identity anchor to the working-tree read -> the manifest-deletion attack wrongly passes), Scenario 21 (drop the deletion enumeration -> the git-rm attack wrongly passes), Scenario 21b (drop --no-renames -> the git-mv attack wrongly passes), Scenario 21c (revert ACMRT to ACMR -> the typechange attack wrongly passes). A mutation proof that does not make its own attack pass again is reported as proving nothing rather than counted as green. Scenario 20 deliberately checks out the attacker's manifest-LESS tree first: the anchor and the deletion arm are redundant against that attack by design, so a mutant judged against a manifest-bearing tree would 'block' for a reason the mutation never touched and the proof would be vacuous. |

NOW EVENT-WIRED IN ITS OWN RIGHT (2026-08-01 starvation fix): settings.json.template carries two direct top-level entries — UserPromptSubmit `touch --event prompt --if-older-than 15` and Stop `touch --event turn-end --if-older-than 15`, both detached (nohup/disown, the limit-resume precedent) so a liveness tick never sits on the operator's critical path. WHY, split by confidence per constitution §1. PROVEN (observable, independently re-derived by harness-reviewer 2026-08-02): the pre-existing in-hook turn-end splice does not run — 535 stop-verdict-dispatcher turn-traces vs 200 workstreams-stop-writer ones, the latter last emitted 2026-07-31T17:18:29Z while the former emitted every turn; session d3059d78 emitted 27 dispatcher turn-traces on 2026-08-01 with ZERO heartbeat updates; all 14 heartbeat files read "last_event":"start", so last_activity_ts was session-START time and the cockpit could never classify any session as currently active. HYPOTHESIZED (mechanism): WHICH kill ends that hook. The first reading — Claude Code's 60s hook timeout — is contradicted by its own evidence (154 of the 200 stop-writer traces recorded total_ms > 60000, max 571816ms, and ledger_emit at workstreams-stop-writer.sh:260 is nine lines BEFORE the touch at :269, so those runs ran past 60s AND reached :260). An equally-consistent mechanism is that the ~43s hb_write at the tail is itself what dies, corroborated by a leaked mktemp file in the real heartbeats dir. REFUTED IF instrumenting the Stop chain shows :269 entered and hb_write returning normally. The fix holds under EITHER mechanism because it removes the dependency on that hook finishing. The splices in session-start-digest.sh / workstreams-stop-writer.sh / pre-compact-continuity.sh / session-resumer.sh remain; note precisely what is and is not collapsed — the two DIRECT entries pass --if-older-than 15 and, with the claim-stake in cmd_touch (which bumps the destination mtime BEFORE hb_write's ~43s fan-out, so a concurrent guard is not blind to an in-flight sibling), genuinely collapse a duplicate between themselves ONCE the session heartbeat file exists -- the first write of a session is NOT collapsed, because the stake cannot create the file without leaving an empty one that every reader parses as JSON (jq exits 4, JSON.parse throws), and two CONCURRENT first-writes therefore do have something to collapse against but cannot; the pre-existing splices pass NO --if-older-than and therefore always write, a duplicate TOLERATED rather than prevented because hb_write is an idempotent atomic overwrite. reap is still called by a best-effort splice in session-start-digest.sh run_digest(), and now also clears orphaned <sid>.json.XXXXXX mktemp leftovers the *.json glob could never match. NOT wired on PostToolUse, deliberately and by measurement (harness-reviewer, 3 runs on the committed blob, LOADED machine 2026-08-02: full hb_write 42267/43011/44834ms, guarded no-op 4675/5809/7147ms, bare bash spawn 509-1106ms) — a per-tool-call site would add 235-1230s per turn; sub-turn liveness belongs in the cockpit's own classifier via the transcript-mtime join hb_is_stale already implements (filed as an nl-issue follow-up). |

Cold-reader-lint WARN (constitution §3 amendment 53d3bee, operator directive 2026-07-07), following FUNCTIONAL-LINK's own precedent immediately above it in this same file: scans the final assistant message for a §3-format "Decision needed" block and, if it is missing an artifact anchor or per-option outcome text, emits ONE ledger_emit warn + a stderr notice. WARN-only — never contributes to the block/gap verdict above, never participates in cycle-counting/DONE-refusal, never touches stdout. Self-tested (scenarios renumbered 20-23 at batch-integration to avoid colliding with the FIX-2a/FIX-2b automation-ceiling scenarios 18-19 already on master; 3 of 4 pass). KNOWN BUG (found during batch integration, confirmed pre-existing on the source branch in isolation, not introduced by the merge): `_svd_message_has_decision_block`'s heuristic does a naive case-insensitive substring match for `decision needed`, so prose that negates it (e.g. "no decision needed here") still matches and false-positive-warns as a decision block missing an anchor — 1 self-test scenario (ordinary-prose-not-scanned) fails on this. Low severity (WARN-only, never blocks) but real; follow-up filed to require the heuristic to exclude a preceding negation token. PROBLEMS-PERSIST WARN (operator directive 2026-07-29, ledger row SURFACED-PROBLEMS-CAN-BE-DROPPED-01, docs/decisions/065-problems-persist-warn-consolidation.md): same non-contributing shape as FUNCTIONAL-LINK/COLD-READER-LINT immediately above them in this file. Scans the final assistant message paragraph-by-paragraph for problem-shaped vocabulary (defect/bug/broken/silently/data loss/root cause) with no inline ledger-ID-shaped token in the same paragraph, and emits ONE ledger_emit warn + a pre-filled `nl-issue.sh "..."` stderr notice per unfiled paragraph. WARN-only — never contributes to the block/gap verdict, never blocks. FP expectation (honest, measured): ordinary engineering prose describing an already-fixed bug in the past tense WILL fire this (measured: 36/1589, ~2.3%, of this repo's own commit-subject vocabulary matches the same regex) — this is why it is WARN not BLOCK. Retirement: narrow the vocabulary or require a corroborating imperative verb if weekly triage shows a low true-catch rate. Self-tested (scenarios 27-30, RED-GREEN proven via mutation: disabling the call site turns exactly the assertions that require the warn to fire red — 80/3 — while the no-warn assertions stay trivially green). VOCABULARY-LOCK WARN (status-event-ledger plan SE10, 2026-07-30, doctrine/claims.md 'Status vocabulary lock'): same non-contributing shape as the three checks above. Scans the final assistant message for an explicit off-vocabulary status-word denylist (e.g. "in flight", "done-ish", "basically done", "wrapping up") that reads as a status claim without being one of the cockpit's six enum values (not-started/in-progress/running/complete/stalled(reason)/unknown(reason)), and emits ONE ledger_emit warn + a stderr notice naming the enum + the fused <PlanKey><TaskId> token convention. WARN-only — never blocks. A bare-numeric task-id check ("task 9" with no plan-key prefix) was drafted and DEFERRED after measurement showed 163/1673 (~9.7%) of this repo's own commit subjects use bare numeric ids for pre-existing plans that never adopted the fused <Key><TaskId> convention — shipping it would warn on ~1 in 10 ordinary reports, failing the "start narrow, high precision" bar; see docs/backlog.md HARNESS-GAP-62 (which also names a SEPARATE, more severe finding from the same investigation: plan-edit-validator.sh's own checkbox-flip TASK_ID regex still rejects fused ids like SE3/RI1 outright, blocking real flips — not fixed here, out of this task's scope). FP expectation for the shipped denylist (measured): 2/1673 (~0.12%) of this repo's own commit subjects. Self-tested (scenarios 31-34, RED-GREEN proven via mutation: disabling the call site turns exactly 2 assertions red — 90/2 — while the no-warn assertions stay trivially green). |
